newsitem.title: USA: Plains cattle market quiet, few $71 bids - trade.
newsitem.headline: Plains cattle market quiet, few $71 bids - trade.

text.p: U.S. central and southern Plains feedlot cattle markets were quiet late Monday morning, with some feedlots passing bids of $70.00 to $71.00 per cwt, feedlot sources said.

The bids were $1.00 to $2.00 lower than the $72.00 top price paid late last week in the central and southern Plains. Feedlot sources said cattle were priced at $73.00, but they expected sales should bids rise to $72.00.
Sales of up to $120.00 per cwt were reported on a dressed basis at Nebraska lots last week and on a live basis, up to $74 to $75, the latter on animals that would grade choice.

Central and southern Plains cattle sources said many of last week's sales should be shipped by Tuesday. Some cattle were shipped Friday, others Monday, and some Kansas yards have cattle slated for shipment Tuesday.

There were instances of a meat packer being granted an extra day to take delivery of cattle. But cattle feeders said lately, several packers had sought extra days only to take delivery sooner than scheduled.
Feedlot sources said $72.00 per cwt prices would be profitable, netting the feedlots about $75.00 to $100.00 per head profit.
Feedlots remain current with this week's showlists containing cattle that could use more days on feed, they said. Several feedlots reported offering cattle with 100 days or less on feed.
"I bet we don't have a pen that has 100 days on it," said a Kansas feedlot source. The cattle averaged 1,100 to 1,150 lbs, she said.
